claims.text: the window was rewritten, not corrected
claims.why: The comment describes a guard condition; the actual anchor checking logic is present in the code, but the exact behavior depends on WINDOW_ANCHOR_FRAC which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Exact line count lets us preserve EACH original terminator, including mixed-EOL fragments and a final unterminated line.
claims.why: The _ending function handles \r\n, \n, \r, and returns empty string for no ending, preserving each original terminator.

claims.text: ``at_eof`` remains in the signature as an explicit caller assertion and for API compatibility.
claims.why: The parameter at_eof is not present in the visible code; it may be in the function signature outside this chunk.

claims.text: Why native and not the OpenAI-compat body: Ollama's /v1/chat/completions shim SILENTLY DROPS an unknown keep_alive field — measured, the TTL stayed at the 5-minute default.
claims.why: This claim refers to behavior of Ollama's API that is not testable from this code chunk.

claims.text: Sending it here is the only thing that actually moves the expiry (verified: expires_at jumped to 30.0 minutes).
claims.why: This is an empirical claim about Ollama's behavior; not verifiable from code.

claims.text: An empty prompt makes this a pure load/refresh (done_reason: "load"), so it costs nothing once the model is already resident.
claims.why: This claim about Ollama's response is not verifiable from this code chunk.
The warm_model function makes an HTTP request to a host which could be remote if OLLAMA_HOST is set to a non-local address, causing network egress.

claims.text: Returns True if the pin was accepted; never raises.
claims.why: The function returns True if status is 2xx, False on exception; it does not raise.
The function starts a daemon thread that runs warm_model.

claims.text: Used to refresh the residency TTL around a chat turn without adding the pin's latency to the user's reply.
claims.why: This describes the intended use; not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: caps above declares local=True, trusted_with_ip=True as STATIC facts about a provider named "ollama". They are not static: host comes from OLLAMA_HOST, so the same class talks to 127.0.0.1 or to an RTX bench across a tailnet with no code change.
claims.why: The caps are class-level constants, but host is determined at runtime from environment variable, making the static caps potentially misleading.
